display_name: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III & Chamaraja Wodeyar X
one_line: Mysore’s nineteenth‑century Wodeyar maharajas, staging royal Dasara spectacle while steering a princely state under British oversight.

appearance.age_look: Two adult men: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III late 40s, slight and scholarly; Chamaraja Wodeyar X mid‑30s, athletic and upright.
appearance.face: Both with warm medium‑brown Mysore complexions and oval faces; Krishnaraja has finer features, small rounded nose, neatly trimmed thin moustache and calm, observant eyes; Chamaraja has a stronger jaw, thicker moustache with slight curl and a steady, determined gaze; default expressions composed and dignified, with a hint of quiet intensity in the eyes.
appearance.hair: Hair mostly hidden under royal Mysore turbans; Krishnaraja wears a compact cream‑gold silk turban wrapped low with a narrow maroon band and a single central gemmed sarpech plume; Chamaraja wears a slightly taller cream‑gold turban with a broader maroon band, a small frontal peak and a three‑feather jewel ornament slightly angled to his right.
appearance.costume: Both wear late‑19th‑century Mysore court achkans: Krishnaraja in a knee‑length, high‑collared cream silk angarkha‑style coat with a gentle flare, fine gold zari floral buta scattered pattern and maroon piping along the placket and cuffs over a plain maroon silk waistcloth and off‑white churidar trousers; Chamaraja in a slightly more structured, straight‑cut cream silk achkan with subtle vertical gold stripes, maroon velvet collar and cuffs, and a narrow maroon sash tied at the waist; Krishnaraja wears a long, sheer maroon silk stole with gold borders draped from his left shoulder across the torso and back, while Chamaraja’s stole is draped from both shoulders like a modest angavastram with matching maroon‑gold borders; both have modest but rich jewellery—double‑strand pearl necklaces with a central emerald pendant, slim gold armlets visible beneath their sleeves, and simple gold rings; footwear is closed, pointed cream‑coloured mojari with maroon edging, fully covering the feet.
appearance.signature: A single ceremonial gold‑hilted Mysore sword with a gently curved steel blade, plain but polished, carried sheathed at Chamaraja’s left hip on a maroon leather belt, while Krishnaraja lightly rests his right hand on the ornate gold pommel shaped with a subtle yali‑head motif.

ref_desc: Two Mysore Wodeyar maharajas stand together: both in cream silk achkans with maroon‑gold stoles, cream‑gold turbans, pearl‑emerald necklaces, cream mojari shoes, and a shared ceremonial gold‑hilted curved sword at Chamaraja’s left hip with Krishnaraja’s hand resting on its pommel.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style character sheet showing two royal Mysore Wodeyar maharajas standing side by side as a single consistent duo: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III slightly shorter and slimmer, in a knee‑length cream silk angarkha‑style coat with fine gold floral buta, maroon piping and off‑white churidar trousers, a maroon silk waistcloth and a long sheer maroon stole with gold borders draped from his left shoulder across the chest; Chamaraja Wodeyar X a little taller and more athletic, in a straight‑cut cream silk achkan with subtle vertical gold stripes, maroon velvet collar and cuffs, a narrow maroon sash at the waist, and a maroon‑gold stole draped from both shoulders like an angavastram; both with warm medium‑brown complexions, oval faces, dignified expressions, slim black moustaches (Krishnaraja’s finer, Chamaraja’s stronger and slightly curled), and cream‑gold silk Mysore turbans with maroon bands and jeweled plume ornaments, Krishnaraja’s turban lower and compact, Chamaraja’s slightly taller with a three‑feather ornament angled right; show modest royal jewellery including double‑strand pearl necklaces with central emerald pendants, slim gold armlets peeking from under sleeves, and simple gold rings; give them closed, pointed cream mojari shoes with maroon edging; include a single polished steel curved ceremonial sword with an ornate gold yali‑head hilt in a maroon scabbard hanging at Chamaraja’s left hip, with Krishnaraja’s right hand resting lightly on its pommel; use a rich but restrained palette of cream, maroon, gold, off‑white and small accents of emerald green, and present them front‑facing in a clean model‑sheet layout that clearly shows their face shapes, turbans, robes, jewellery and the shared sword design for consistent redrawing.
